messages:
marta: customers in prod-us-east are hitting intermittent 504s and 5xxs during tenant burst, escalated by support. started ~10:03 UTC.
ryan: looking now — is this the tenant that did the large batch import?
marta: yes, tenant-731 did a 50k embedding import at 10:02. latency spiked and gateway returned 504s after ~30s. support saw auth 401s earlier that recovered.
sam_oncall: pulled gateway logs — I see a backlog of socket connections and handler timeouts. snippet:```
2025-10-01T10:03:28Z gateway inference-gateway[2378]: warn: request stalled, queue_len=312, active_workers=12
2025-10-01T10:03:29Z gateway inference-gateway[2378]: error: upstream timeout to backend (504) tenant=tenant-731
```
ryan: that queue_len and active_workers ratio smells like slow scale-up. what's the HPA/KEDA status?
marta: current scaledobject shows cooldown=300s and minReplicaCount=1, pollingInterval=30. KEDA metrics show no additional scaled pods spawning for 90s.
ryan: can you paste the scaledobject?
marta: ```
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: ScaledObject
metadata:
  name: so-tenant-731
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    name: inference-deployment
  pollingInterval: 30
  cooldownPeriod: 300
  minReplicaCount: 1
  triggers:
  - type: redis
    metadata:
      listName: requests-tenant-731
      listLength: "10"
```
sam_oncall: cooldown 300 is pretty long; also minReplicaCount 1 means coldstart if existing workers are busy. we usually set prewarm replicas or a lower cooldown for high-throughput tenants.
ryan: also check readinessProbe for inference pods — if probe is strict and model init takes 60s, pods won't serve even if scheduled. we had a launch-time quantization path that delayed readiness.
marta: pod describe shows initContainer model-fetch took ~18s and main container reported readiness after 52s. readiness probe configured as `httpGet /health?full` with failureThreshold=3, period=10.
support: customer reported retries from client on SDK side, they hit 5xx and then auth 401s when token rotation happened. billing spikes noted but no quota blocks.
ryan: two vectors: KEDA/HPA mis-tuned + slow model init -> warmup delay -> socket queueing -> gateway 504. Repro steps?
sam_oncall: quick repro: flood the tenant with concurrent requests (50 concurrent embeddings) while scaling pool to 1 replica. I ran: `siege -c50 -t30S https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings` with tenant header and saw 40% 504.
marta: adding logs from keda-operator:```
2025-10-01T10:03:15Z keda-operator: debug: metric fetch ok
2025-10-01T10:03:18Z keda-operator: warn: skipping scale, cooldown not elapsed for scaledobject so-tenant-731
```
ryan: suggested mitigation: 1) bump minReplicaCount to 3 for this tenant or enable dedicated prewarm pool; 2) lower cooldown to 60s; 3) change readiness probe to a lightweight `tcp` or `/health?ready` that doesn't wait on full model warming; 4) add KV/prefix caching for embedding imports to smooth load.
marta: opening infra change now for ephemeral prewarm on that tenant and lowering cooldown. patch: `kubectl patch scaledobject so-tenant-731 -p '{"spec":{"minReplicaCount":3,"cooldownPeriod":60}}'`
support: created customer ticket RED-45321 and notified customer that we're applying mitigations.
deploy-bot: deployment inference-deployment scaled to 3 replicas (triggered by operator) — rollout 10:12 UTC :rocket:
ryan: follow-up actions: add an alert for socket_queue_len > 200, update onboarding docs to recommend scaledobject defaults for large imports, and schedule a postmortem if we see recurrence.
sam_oncall: I'll add a temporary synthetic load test to run 24h to validate behavior.
marta: closing thread for now, will update once customer confirms stabilization. :white_check_mark:
